note: Promotion to the tracked schema (roadmap Phase 1 backfill). Track groups follow the (XX) prefixes already embedded in the source theme names. Empty fields (track, code, level, description) are filled; authored transfer_check values replace ONLY the two known generic placeholder sentences — real source checks are never overwritten (guard in tools/normalize_blocks.py).

themes.description: Supporting the head, the safe carries and the safe sleep position — handling an infant with confidence.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate safe holds, head support and the safe sleep position on a doll or supervised infant, faultlessly.

themes.description: The short list behind crying — hunger, wind, tiredness, discomfort — worked through in order before despair.
themes.transfer_check: Given a crying scenario, work the short list in order — hunger, wind, tiredness, discomfort — narrating each check.

themes.description: How infants are fed and the practicalities of each — hunger cues, hygiene, and support for the person feeding.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate one feeding method's full hygiene and technique, and state the support the feeding person needs.

themes.description: What infant sleep actually looks like, the safe sleep rules, and surviving the nights as a household.
themes.transfer_check: Set up a safe infant sleep space correctly and design a survivable night rota for a real or case-study household.

themes.theme: Talking to somebody who cannot talk back (IN)
themes.description: Why narration, songs and responses build a brain — serving conversation before there are words.
themes.transfer_check: Record ten minutes of narrated interaction with an infant — naming, responding, singing — and note each response you served.

themes.theme: When a parent is not coping (IN)
themes.description: Exhaustion and low mood after a baby — the signs, the words to use, and the help that exists.
themes.transfer_check: Role-play the conversation with an exhausted parent: the signs named kindly, and one real source of help offered.

themes.description: What play does for development at each stage, and playing with a baby using what a home already has.
themes.transfer_check: Run three age-matched play activities using only what a home already has, and say what each builds.

themes.description: What vaccines do, the schedule where you live, and answering a worried question with the evidence.
themes.transfer_check: Present the actual schedule where you live and answer one sceptical question with the evidence, calmly.

themes.theme: The home that is safe enough (IN)
themes.description: The hazards at a crawling child's height — water, heat, poisons, falls — found and fixed room by room.
themes.transfer_check: Audit one real home at crawling height — water, heat, poisons, falls — and fix or flag every finding.

themes.description: What an older child can genuinely do for a baby, and the jobs that stay with adults.
themes.transfer_check: List what an older child can genuinely do for a baby and what stays with adults, and demonstrate two of the child's jobs.

themes.description: The ordinary range of growing up — bodies, moods, abilities — and the changes worth a professional look.
themes.transfer_check: For a named age, sort a list of behaviours and changes into ordinary range versus worth-a-check, with reasons.

themes.theme: A child who is struggling at school (CH)
themes.description: Reading the signs behind falling behind — sight, hearing, home, bullying — before concluding laziness.
themes.transfer_check: For a case-study struggling child, list the checks that come before the laziness conclusion, in order, with who does each.

themes.description: What screens give and take at each age, and household rules that are followed because they are fair.
themes.transfer_check: Draft household screen rules with the young people they bind, fair enough that they sign them.

themes.description: How friendships form and fail through childhood, and helping a lonely child without engineering their life.
themes.transfer_check: For a case-study lonely child, propose support that creates chances without engineering, and the sign that it is working.

themes.theme: The body a teenager is getting used to (CH)
themes.description: Puberty as it actually unfolds — timing, variation, feelings — and being askable when questions come.
themes.transfer_check: Answer three typical puberty questions accurately and comfortably at the level of the asker.

themes.description: Why adolescents seek risk, the difference between growth risks and harm, and steering without forbidding everything.
themes.transfer_check: Sort ten adolescent risks into growth-risk and harm-risk, and design one supervised growth-risk properly.

themes.description: When trouble arrives — school, police, substances — the adult response that helps in the first 24 hours.
themes.transfer_check: Walk the first 24 hours of a case-study trouble scenario — who is called, what is said, what is not — in order.

themes.description: First earnings and spending — helping a teenager run real money with real mistakes at a survivable size.
themes.transfer_check: Design a real-money arrangement for a teenager — income, obligations, survivable mistakes — and review it with one.

themes.description: The skills audit before independence — cooking, money, paperwork — and the leaving that keeps the door open.
themes.transfer_check: Run the full skills audit on a real or case-study school-leaver and set the plan that closes the two worst gaps.

themes.description: Giving a young person genuine responsibility — sized to stretch, supervised lightly, and owned by them.
themes.transfer_check: Hand a young person one genuine sized responsibility, supervise it lightly, and debrief what they owned.

themes.description: The checks and symptoms adults defer — and the short list that should never wait for a quiet month.
themes.transfer_check: List the checks adults defer, identify which are due for a real adult (yourself included), and book or diarise one.

themes.theme: Working with a body that hurts (AD)
themes.description: Working life with pain — pacing, adjustments and the difference between soreness and damage.
themes.transfer_check: For a real or case-study working adult in pain, produce the paced plan that distinguishes soreness from damage.

themes.theme: Being the person everybody depends on (AD)
themes.description: Carrying a household, a job and other people's needs — the load named honestly and shared deliberately.
themes.transfer_check: Map one real adult's full load — work, care, household — and redistribute two items deliberately, with agreement.

themes.theme: A partner, a household, a plan (AD)
themes.description: Running a shared life on purpose — money, work, care and the conversations that keep them agreed.
themes.transfer_check: Run the household planning conversation — money, work, care — to a written one-page agreement both keep.

themes.description: Job loss handled in order — money triage, entitlements, the search — and the identity blow named as real.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the first-fortnight plan for a case-study job loss: money triage, entitlements checked, the search begun.

themes.theme: The friend who has stopped answering (AD)
themes.description: Noticing withdrawal in an adult friend and reaching them without ambush or retreat.
themes.transfer_check: Script and role-play the reach-out to a withdrawn friend — without ambush, without retreat — through to an offer made.

themes.description: What grief does to a person and a household, what helps, and the support that fits each age.
themes.transfer_check: For three ages, state what grief commonly looks like and what helps, and draft one real condolence done well.

themes.description: The documents an adult life runs on — ID, insurance, wills, records — organised so someone else could find them.
themes.transfer_check: Organise one real adult's document set — ID, insurance, records, wishes — findable by somebody else in ten minutes.

themes.description: Retraining and starting again mid-life — the routes that exist, the costs, and the transferable skills already held.
themes.transfer_check: Map one real mid-life retraining route — cost, duration, first step — against the skills already held.

themes.theme: Being somebody a young person can call (AD)
themes.description: Mentoring without a program — being a safe, steady adult a young person can actually reach.
themes.transfer_check: Establish or rehearse the mentoring arrangement: the availability stated, the boundaries set, the first conversation held.

themes.description: What ordinary ageing changes — strength, senses, speed — and what is illness rather than age.
themes.transfer_check: Sort a list of later-life changes into ordinary ageing versus illness-to-check, and say where the check happens locally.

themes.description: Why falls end independence, the home hazards behind most of them, and the strength work that prevents them.
themes.transfer_check: Audit one real older person's home for fall hazards, fix or flag each, and teach one strength exercise correctly.

themes.description: The adaptations, services and routines that keep an older person safely in their own home longer.
themes.transfer_check: Specify the adaptations and services that would keep a real or case-study elder home safely for another year, costed roughly.

themes.description: Ordinary forgetting versus concerning change, the assessment path, and living well alongside dementia.
themes.transfer_check: For a case-study memory change, distinguish ordinary forgetting from concerning signs and map the local assessment path.

themes.description: What isolation does to health, and the contact — visits, calls, groups — that measurably protects.
themes.transfer_check: Establish one real recurring contact for an isolated older person — visit, call, group — and keep it for a month.

themes.description: Pensions, entitlements and the scams aimed at older people — later-life money protected and claimed.
themes.transfer_check: Check one real or case-study elder's entitlements against what is actually claimed, and flag the two scams most aimed at them.

themes.description: Receiving care while keeping choice and privacy — what dignity in care concretely requires.
themes.transfer_check: Observe or role-play one care interaction and mark where choice and privacy were kept or lost, with the fix for each loss.

themes.description: Raising driving, safely and kindly, with evidence — and the alternatives that keep a life mobile.
themes.transfer_check: Role-play the driving conversation with evidence and kindness, ending with two real mobility alternatives arranged.

themes.description: Drawing out and recording the skills and stories an older person holds before they are lost.
themes.transfer_check: Record one older person's skill or story properly — audio or written — and archive it where the family can reach it.

themes.description: Working past pension age — the rights, the adjustments and the roles where experience outweighs speed.
themes.transfer_check: For one real or case-study older worker, list the rights and adjustments that apply and draft the request for one.

themes.description: Recognising yourself as a carer — the role named, the entitlements it unlocks, and the support registered for.
themes.transfer_check: Complete the carer self-identification: the role named, the local register or support service found, the first contact made.

themes.description: Moving a person safely for both of you — technique, aids and the moves never done alone.
themes.transfer_check: Demonstrate one safe assisted transfer with correct technique on a consenting partner, and name the moves never done alone.

themes.description: Managing another person's medicines — schedule, storage, records — and the errors the system must prevent.
themes.transfer_check: Set up a real or simulated medication system — schedule, storage, record — that catches a deliberately planted error.

themes.theme: The carer who is not sleeping (CR)
themes.description: Care that breaks the carer's nights — the risks of running empty and the fixes worth fighting for.
themes.transfer_check: For a real or case-study carer, chart a fortnight of actual rest and secure one concrete change that protects a night.

themes.description: Breaks that actually restore — arranging cover you trust and taking the time without guilt.
themes.transfer_check: Arrange or fully plan one genuine respite break — cover trusted, handover written, the time actually taken.

themes.theme: Caring for somebody who does not want it (CR)
themes.description: Refusal, pride and risk — caring within another adult's right to decide, and when safety overrides.
themes.transfer_check: Role-play care within refusal: the person's right to decide respected, the safety line named, the compromise found.

themes.description: What dying looks like, what comfort care does, and being present in the last days without panic.
themes.transfer_check: Describe what dying commonly looks like and demonstrate two comfort measures, staying present through a role-played hour.

themes.description: The first week's duties — certification, notification, the funeral — and the support for the person left.
themes.transfer_check: Produce the first-week checklist — certification, notifications, the funeral, the person left — for a case-study death, in order.

themes.description: Paid care as skilled work — the training, the standards and the routes into it locally.
themes.transfer_check: Map the real local routes into paid care work — training, certification, starting pay — from actual providers.

themes.description: The carer's own health, network and plan — kept deliberately, because the caring depends on it.
themes.transfer_check: Write your own or a case-study carer's support plan — health, network, backup — and activate one element of it.
